authority.physicsBoundary: Current real-world physics does not establish nondestructive arbitrary many-body quantum-state tomography or this storage behavior. Q-channel carrier identity and its reconstruction physics are Black Light setting technology and may not be presented as contemporary science.

scanDomain.boundaryRule: The Q-map is a bounded state description. Correlations whose partner state extends beyond Omega_R are stored as open-edge dependencies with uncertainty/reference metadata rather than falsely represented as completely known internal state.

stateRepresentation.principle: The Q-map file is a generative relational description, not an explicit classical table containing an independent amplitude/value for every atomic or subatomic degree of freedom. It stores reconstructive constraints, correlations, local generators, boundary conditions, uncertainty, cross-channel structure, and a Q-reference key.

compressionParadox.naiveScaling: For N generic d-level subsystems, a naive arbitrary state description grows approximately as d^N in state-space burden.
compressionParadox.qMapScaling: S_Q is modeled as scaling with the number of resolved relational domains, graph edges, constraint rank, boundary complexity, and residual entropy rather than with a naive exhaustive enumeration of the full Hilbert-space basis.
compressionParadox.informationAccounting: I_reconstruction = I_file + I_Q-reference + I_constraints/laws. The disturbing feature is that I_Q-reference appears to be physically available to the reconstruction process rather than stored as an ordinary external dictionary of comparable size.
compressionParadox.scientificProblem: Conventional computer scientists expect the apparently missing information to exist in a hidden dictionary, oracle, decoder state, training corpus, or lossy approximation. Mature Q-maps can pass reconstruction and covariance tests without exposing such a conventional side-information reservoir. The unresolved question is whether the file is extraordinarily compressed or whether Q-physics itself supplies part of the decompression basis.

neuralMapping.temporalRule: Neural Q-mapping requires a substantially tighter acquisition-time covariance than static machinery mapping because a brain is a rapidly changing electrochemical system. A neural map records a bounded temporal state estimate, not an eternal exact object.

constraints.text: Increasing scan radius, penetration depth, spatial resolution, temporal resolution, and Q-relational resolution cannot all be improved independently without increasing energy, aperture, sensor count, time, control bandwidth, or uncertainty burden.
Entanglement across the scan boundary creates open relational edges. The scanner must preserve them as unresolved dependencies rather than claiming omniscience outside the scan volume.

Measurement back-action must be represented. Higher technology can reduce, characterize, reverse, or compensate portions of the disturbance but does not make measurement consequence-free by declaration.
A compact stored map can still require a sophisticated reconstruction engine and a valid Q-reference environment. File size and reconstruction complexity are separate engineering quantities.
Q-reference compatibility may behave as a physical key: a map can be structurally intact yet unreconstructable at full fidelity if its reference relationship cannot be reproduced or translated.
The exact particle, field, interaction, or carrier used by the Q-state interrogation channel is not currently named by surviving authority and must not be fabricated as recovered canon.

failureModes.text: Reference drift: phase/reference state changes during acquisition, producing a map that is internally precise but registered to the wrong Q basis.
Boundary truncation: significant outside-volume dependencies are omitted or underweighted, creating false confidence in a locally reconstructed state.
Temporal decoherence: target evolution exceeds acquisition synchronization, especially in neural or active-machine scans, producing mutually incompatible temporal slices.
Cross-channel misregistration: resonance, penetrating, and Q channels are spatially or temporally offset and compile into a self-consistent but physically wrong reconstruction.
Dense-material or shielding shadow: one or more classical structural channels become poorly conditioned, increasing the burden placed on relational reconstruction.
Q-reference spoof: a hostile or corrupted reference can cause valid measurements to compile against an incorrect relational basis.
False-low entropy solution: the compiler finds an extremely compact relational model that satisfies sampled checks but discards physically significant unresolved structure.
Back-action excursion: probe interaction perturbs the target beyond the certified post-scan disturbance envelope.
